models.name: economic_discussion_citizens
models.description:
Registered citizen accounts with email/password authentication credentials and profile information including display name and bio.

Each citizen can register with a unique email and password, manage their profile by editing their display name and bio, and interact with the system by creating articles and writing comments. Citizns are the foundational user type who can request administrator status.

This table stores authentication credentials securely using bcrypt password hashing. Profile data is kept separate from session persistence and password reset mechanisms that are handled in companion tables.

All citizen accounts are subject to hard deletion (not soft deletion) when users explicitly request account removal, which triggers the permanent removal of all associated articles and comments.

Citizens have no administrative privileges and are restricted to viewing content, creating articles/comments, and managing their own profile.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for authentication and communication. Must be valid according to RFC 5322 standards and unique across all citizens.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Cryptographically hashed password using bcrypt algorithm. Never stores plain text passwords. Used for authentication during login.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Public display name shown to other users. Used in article and comment attribution. Must be between 1 and 100 characters.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional biography or personal description provided by the citizen. Can be edited at any time. Limited to 500 characters.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the citizen account was created. Set once at registration and never modified.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the citizen's profile information (display name or bio). Updated automatically on each profile modification.

models.name: economic_discussion_citizen_sessions
models.description: Tracks login sessions for citizen users. Each session represents one authentication event with associated connection context and expiration timing.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Citizen's {@link economic_discussion_citizens.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address from which the session was initialized.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the initial page requested during session creation.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL captured at session creation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session expires. Sessions must expire for security; unlimited sessions are prohibited unless explicitly requested.

models.name: economic_discussion_citizen_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for citizen account recovery workflows.

Each token is generated when a citizen requests a password reset and is used exactly once to verify identity and reset credentials. The system enforces secure password recovery by requiring tokens to expire within a defined period.

Tokens are single-use - after successful password reset, the token becomes invalid and is not reused. The token value is cryptographically generated and sufficiently random to prevent brute force attacks.

This table supports secure password recovery without exposing user credentials and prevents token replay attacks by enforcing expiration. All tokens are linked to a specific citizen account for auditability.

No soft delete is used as reset tokens have finite lifespans and are purged automatically upon expiration or after use. The system retains token records for audit trail purposes until expiration.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who requested the password reset. {@link economic_discussion_citizens.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique cryptographically secure token for password reset. Must be globally unique and unguessable. Used to verify the identity of the requesting citizen.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the password reset token. Session must expire to prevent abuse. All tokens have a fixed expiration time for security.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token was generated and issued to the user.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token was last modified (typically updated when token is used or invalidated).

models.name: economic_discussion_administrators
models.description:
Administrator accounts with elevated privileges for content and user moderation, authenticated via email/password.

Represents users who have been granted administrative rights to moderate content, manage sections, and enforce community guidelines. Administrators retain the capabilities of regular citizens (creating articles, commenting) with additional permissions for deletion, banning, and section management. Each administrator is formally promoted from a citizen account through a request and approval workflow.

This table contains core authentication credentials (email and password hash), profile data (display name and bio), and temporal fields for auditing. It serves as the authoritative identity record for the administrator actor type. The relationship with economic_discussion_citizens establishes identity inheritance, ensuring seamless transition from regular user to administrator status, while economic_discussion_administrator_sessions manages active login sessions.

All administrative actions performed via the system are logged with this administrator’s identity as the source.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Base citizen identity record this administrator was promoted from. {@link economic_discussion_citizens.id}.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Administrator email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique system-wide.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: bcrypt-hashed password for secure authentication. Never stored in plain text.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Public-facing name displayed to other users. Override for the base citizen display name if changed.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional biography or profile description provided by the administrator.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this administrator account was created (promotion date).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp last updated (profile edit, password change, etc.).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when administrator account was soft-deleted. If null, account is active.

models.name: economic_discussion_administrator_sessions
models.description:
Tracks login sessions for administrator actors. Records connection context and authentication state for auditing and security.

Each session represents a single successful administrator login event. The session is active from created_at until expired_at, at which point it becomes invalid. Administrators may have multiple concurrent sessions.

This table is essential for maintaining secure authentication state. Connection metadata (IP, referrer) helps detect suspicious activity. Sessions are automatically expired by the system and can be revoked by administrators.

This table is replenished with new sessions on successful login and does not support CRUD operations from users. Its data is managed entirely by the authentication system.

foreignFields.name: administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Administrator's {@link economic_discussion_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: The IP address from which the session was initiated.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: The URL of the page from which the login request originated.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: The referrer URL in the HTTP request header at time of login.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The exact time when this session was created (UTC).

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: The time when this session expires and becomes invalid. Sessions MUST expire for security; this field cannot be null.

models.name: economic_discussion_administrator_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for administrators, used to securely recover access to their accounts.

This table stores cryptographic tokens issued when an administrator initiates a password reset request. Each token is single-use and expires after a limited duration. The system generates and validates tokens programmatically during the password recovery workflow, never exposing them to users directly in the UI.

Tokens are created when an administrator requests password reset, invalidated when used to reset the password, and automatically purged after expiration. The table ensures that only legitimate, in-flight password reset requests can alter account credentials.

This is a supporting entity for the administrator actor system and should not be directly accessed or modified by application logic outside the authentication service.

foreignFields.name: economic_discussion_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator account this reset token belongs to. {@link economic_discussion_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique cryptographic token used to authenticate the password reset request. Must be stored in encoded format and verified during reset.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the reset token. After this time, the token becomes invalid and cannot be used. Must be non-null to ensure security.

plainFields.name: used
plainFields.description: Indicates whether this reset token has already been consumed to reset the password. Once true, no further operations can use this token.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the reset token was generated and issued to the administrator.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this record, typically updated when the 'used' field is set to true.

models.name: economic_discussion_super_administrators
models.description:
Super administrator accounts with highest system privileges including promotion/demotion rights, authenticated via email/password.

Represents the highest authority level in the system, capable of managing all administrator promotions and demotions. Unlike regular administrators, super administrators can elevate other administrators to super administrator status and demote super administrators (but not themselves). This entity serves as the root of the privilege hierarchy and requires strict authentication with secure password hashing.

Each super administrator account is associated with a unique email address for login and a password hash for authentication security. The account retains standard profile fields including display name and bio for personalization. All super administrator accounts are subject to the same soft delete capability as other actors, preserving audit trails while allowing for account removal when necessary.

This actor type must have its own dedicated session table (economic_discussion_super_administrator_sessions) and password reset table (economic_discussion_super_administrator_password_resets) to maintain separation of concerns and security domains.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Unique email address used for authentication and system communications. Must be valid per RFC 5322 standard and unique across all actor types.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: bcrypt hash of the user's password. Never store plain text passwords. Required for login authentication functionality.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Public-facing name for the super administrator. Used in UI displays, notifications, and audit trails. Must be non-empty and suitable for public display.

plainFields.name: bio
plainFields.description: Optional personal bio or description provided by the super administrator. Limited to 500 characters for brevity and readability. May contain basic formatting for profile presentation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the super administrator account was created. Automatically set by the system upon registration.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the super administrator account (profile changes, password reset, etc.). Automatically updated by the system.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. If null, account is active. If set, account is marked as deleted and cannot be used for authentication. This preserves audit trails while logically removing access.

models.name: economic_discussion_super_administrator_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for super administrator authentication with access and refresh token support.

Tracks login sessions for super administrators with complete connection context including IP address, connection URL, and referrer information. Each session represents a distinct authentication event and is associated with exactly one super administrator account.

Sessions are append-only audit trails that record when and from where a super administrator logged in. All sessions have an expiration time to enforce security policies - sessions cannot remain active indefinitely.

The session data is used for security monitoring, detecting unauthorized access patterns, and maintaining compliance with authentication standards. Super administrators can have multiple concurrent sessions.

This table strictly follows the session pattern: no additional fields beyond the required specification, no updates to existing records, and no soft deletion of session records.

foreignFields.name: super_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: Associated super administrator account. {@link economic_discussion_super_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the device used to initiate the session.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL of the connection endpoint that initiated this session.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: Referrer URL that led the user to this application.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session was created.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the session will expire. Sessions must expire for security - this field is NOT NULL.

models.name: economic_discussion_super_administrator_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens for super administrators with expiration and usage tracking.

This table stores temporary tokens used for secure password recovery of super administrator accounts. Each token is single-use, has a limited expiration period, and is automatically invalidated after use. The system generates these tokens when super administrators request password resets, and the tokens are consumed during the password reset process.

Tokens are bound to a specific super administrator via the super_administrator_id foreign key, ensuring that reset requests are tied to the correct account. The used flag prevents token reuse, which is a critical security feature. The expires_at field enforces time-bound security, ensuring tokens cannot be used indefinitely. This table is managed entirely by the authentication system and is never directly accessed or modified by end users.

All records in this table are temporary and expected to be cleaned up after expiration or use. No permanent user data is stored here, only ephemeral authentication artifacts that support secure password recovery workflows.

foreignFields.name: super_administrator_id
foreignFields.description: The super administrator associated with this password reset token. {@link economic_discussion_super_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description: Unique, cryptographically secure token string used for password reset. This value is sent to the super administrator through secure channels (email) and must be presented to complete password reset.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: Expiration timestamp for the password reset token. Tokens are valid only until this time, after which they become invalid and cannot be used for password reset.

plainFields.name: used
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether this reset token has been used to change a password. Once true, the token is invalidated and cannot be used again.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this password reset token was generated and issued to the super administrator.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to this record, typically when the token is marked as used.

models.name: economic_discussion_configurations
models.description:
System-wide configuration settings including feature flags, performance thresholds, and operational parameters.

This singleton table stores essential operational parameters that control the behavior of the entire Economic/Political Discussion Board system.
All values in this table are system configuration settings that determine functionality, performance limits, and operational constraints.

This table serves as the authoritative source for feature enablement, rate limits, search thresholds, and system behavior control.
Changes to these settings require administrative access and are typically managed by the DevOps team through deployment pipelines rather than runtime interfaces.

The table contains boolean flags for feature enablement, numeric thresholds for performance optimization, and string parameters for operational configuration.
All values are persisted and persist across application restarts.

This table is the configuration backbone of the entire system, determining what features are available, how the system performs under load, and how various components behave.

Note: This table is classified as primary since it's the authoritative configuration source, even though not directly managed by end-users.

The table includes:
- Feature flags for enabling/disabling system capabilities
- Performance thresholds for search, upload, and response times
- Operational parameters for file size limits, connection rates, and caching
- Tracking fields for audit purposes (created_at, updated_at)

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was created (immutable).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this configuration was last modified.

plainFields.name: search_enabled
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether full-text search functionality is enabled system-wide.

plainFields.name: article_search_threshold
plainFields.description: Minimum number of characters required in search query to trigger full-text search (prevents overly broad queries).

plainFields.name: search_result_limit
plainFields.description: Maximum number of search results to return per page.

plainFields.name: file_upload_enabled
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether file uploads (for articles) are enabled system-wide.

plainFields.name: max_file_size_mb
plainFields.description: Maximum file size allowed for uploads in megabytes (enforces 50MB limit per file).

plainFields.name: max_files_per_article
plainFields.description: Maximum number of files/images allowed per article (enforces 5-file limit).

plainFields.name: comment_enabled
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether comments on articles are enabled system-wide.

plainFields.name: min_comment_length
plainFields.description: Minimum character length required for a comment (enforces 5-character minimum).

plainFields.name: max_comment_length
plainFields.description: Maximum character length allowed for a comment (enforces 1,000-character limit).

plainFields.name: admin_request_enabled
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether citizens can submit requests to become administrators.

plainFields.name: ban_reason_required
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether a ban reason is mandatory when banning users (enforces 10-character minimum).

plainFields.name: max_sessions_per_user
plainFields.description: Maximum number of concurrent sessions allowed per user (enforces reasonable session limits).

plainFields.name: session_expiry_hours
plainFields.description: Number of hours before a session expires (sets cookie/JWT expiry time).

plainFields.name: cache_enabled
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether client-side caching is enabled for improved performance.

plainFields.name: cache_ttl_seconds
plainFields.description: Time to live for cached content in seconds. Sets duration for static content caching.

plainFields.name: maintenance_mode
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether the system is in maintenance mode (disables most user features).

plainFields.name: email_notification_enabled
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether system emails (password resets, notifications) are enabled.

plainFields.name: email_smtp_host
plainFields.description: SMTP host address for outgoing email notifications. Configured by system administrator.

plainFields.name: email_smtp_port
plainFields.description: SMTP port address for outgoing email notifications. Typically 587 or 465.

plainFields.name: email_smtp_username
plainFields.description: Username for SMTP authentication when sending system emails.

plainFields.name: email_sender_name
plainFields.description: Display name used in system-generated emails (e.g., "Economic Discussion Board").

plainFields.name: email_sender_address
plainFields.description: Email address used as sender for system-generated emails (e.g., "noreply@economicsite.com").

plainFields.name: search_trigram_enabled
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether PostgreSQL GIN trigram indexes are enabled for fuzzy search support.

plainFields.name: search_fuzzy_threshold
plainFields.description: Minimum similarity threshold (0.0-1.0) for fuzzy matching in search queries. Higher = more exact matches.

plainFields.name: auto_archive_old_comments
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether system automatically archives old comments after 1 year (for performance).

plainFields.name: auto_archive_days
plainFields.description: Number of days after which comments are considered "old" and eligible for archiving.

plainFields.name: max_articles_per_section
plainFields.description: Maximum number of articles allowed in a single section before warning the administrator of potential overload.

plainFields.name: max_tags_per_article
plainFields.description: Maximum number of tags allowed per article (enforces 10-tag limit).

plainFields.name: auto_tag_suggestions
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether system should suggest tags to users as they type.

plainFields.name: rate_limit_requests_per_minute
plainFields.description: Maximum number of requests allowed per minute per IP address (enforces 100 requests per minute limit).

plainFields.name: rate_limit_login_attempts
plainFields.description: Maximum number of login attempts allowed per email address within 15 minutes.

plainFields.name: max_admin_actions_per_minute
plainFields.description: Maximum number of administrator actions (ban/delete) allowed per minute per admin to prevent abuse.

plainFields.name: audit_logs_enabled
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether all critical system actions are logged for security auditing.

plainFields.name: audit_log_retention_days
plainFields.description: Number of days to retain audit logs before auto-deletion of old records.

plainFields.name: data_retention_enabled
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether the data retention policy is enforced to keep banned users' content.

plainFields.name: content_backups_enabled
plainFields.description: Flag indicating whether automated backups of content are performed daily.

plainFields.name: backup_retention_days
plainFields.description: Number of days to retain automated content backups before deletion.

plainFields.name: feature_flag_new_ui
plainFields.description: Experimental feature flag for enabling new UI components (not used in production yet).

plainFields.name: feature_flag_api_v2
plainFields.description: Experimental feature flag for enabling v2 API endpoints (not used in production yet).

plainFields.name: feature_flag_community_moderation
plainFields.description: Experimental feature flag enabling community moderation features (not used in production yet).

plainFields.name: feature_flag_ai_recommendations
plainFields.description: Experimental feature flag enabling AI-powered article recommendations (not used in production yet).

plainFields.name: feature_flag_dark_mode
plainFields.description: Feature flag enabling dark mode interface for all users.

plainFields.name: feature_flag_language_support
plainFields.description: Feature flag enabling multi-language support for content (English only currently).

plainFields.name: feature_flag_mobile_app
plainFields.description: Feature flag enabling mobile app integration and features.

plainFields.name: feature_flag_email_digest
plainFields.description: Feature flag enabling daily email digests of article activity.

plainFields.name: feature_flag_emoji_reactions
plainFields.description: Feature flag enabling emoji reactions on comments.

plainFields.name: feature_flag_pinned_articles
plainFields.description: Feature flag enabling administrators to pin important articles to top of section.

plainFields.name: feature_flag_topic_following
plainFields.description: Feature flag enabling users to follow specific discussion topics.

plainFields.name: feature_flag_user_badges
plainFields.description: Feature flag enabling user achievement badges for participation.

plainFields.name: feature_flag_search_history
plainFields.description: Feature flag enabling users to view their past search queries.

plainFields.name: feature_flag_profile_views
plainFields.description: Feature flag enabling users to see who viewed their profile.

plainFields.name: feature_flag_privacy_mode
plainFields.description: Feature flag enabling users to hide their online status.

models.name: economic_discussion_component_statuses
models.description:
Status tracking for application components (search engine, file storage, email service) with health indicators and last check timestamps.

This table monitors the operational health of critical system components. Each record represents the current status of a specific system component, with the most recent check timestamp and any error details from the last health check.

The system automatically updates these records periodically through health monitoring services. Administrators use this data to identify failing components and troubleshoot infrastructure issues.

Relationship: Each component status is linked to a specific configuration in economic_discussion_configurations.

Status values are typically: 'healthy', 'degraded', 'critical', 'unknown'.

No soft delete required as component status records are updated rather than deleted.

This table is classified as subsidiary because it supports the economic_discussion_configurations table and is managed by system infrastructure, not direct user interaction.

foreignFields.name: economic_discussion_configurations_id
foreignFields.description: Configuration record for this component. {@link economic_discussion_configurations.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp in UTC.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp in UTC.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current health status of the component. Valid values: 'healthy', 'degraded', 'critical', 'unknown'.

plainFields.name: last_check_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last health check performed for this component.

plainFields.name: error_message
plainFields.description: Error message from the most recent health check, if any. Empty string if no error occurred.

models.name: economic_discussion_deployment_metadata
models.description:
Metadata about system versions, build times, and deployment information for audit and diagnostics.

Stores immutable deployment records for version control, debugging, and operational audit. Each record represents a single deployment event and captures the exact software version, build timestamp, deployment timestamp, git commit hash, environment, and additional metadata for diagnostic purposes. Records are append-only and permanently retained as part of system audit history.

This table is managed by the deployment pipeline, not by users. It has no direct user interaction, no editing capability, and no role-based permissions since it's purely operational metadata for internal diagnostics and changelog generation.

plainFields.name: version
plainFields.description: Application version number in semver format (e.g., "1.2.3").

plainFields.name: build_time
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when the application was built.

plainFields.name: deployment_time
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this version was deployed to the target environment.

plainFields.name: git_commit
plainFields.description: Full git commit hash that was built and deployed.

plainFields.name: env
plainFields.description: Target deployment environment (e.g., "production", "staging", "development").

plainFields.name: additional_metadata
plainFields.description: JSON-formatted string containing optional additional deployment metadata (e.g., CI pipeline URL, build server info, custom tags).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this deployment record was created in the database.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this deployment record was last updated (always equals created_at as records are immutable).

models.name: economic_discussion_sections
models.description:
Stores section metadata including name, description, creation/modification timestamps, and deletion status. Each section serves as a top-level category for organizing articles.

Sections are managed exclusively by administrators and provide the organizational structure for article content. Users can browse and filter articles by section, but only administrators can create, edit, or delete sections. Section names must be unique and follow naming conventions (alphanumeric, spaces, hyphens, underscores). The description provides additional context about the section's scope and purpose.

When a section is deleted, it is marked with deleted_at timestamp rather than being physically removed, preserving historical article-to-section relationships while hiding the section from active listings. All section modifications are tracked through created_at and updated_at fields which record the exact moment of creation and last edit.

Section name and description fields are validated during creation and edit operations to ensure they meet minimum and maximum character length requirements (name: 3-50 characters, description: 50-500 characters).

foreignFields.name: created_by_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who created this section. {@link economic_discussion_administrators.id}.

foreignFields.name: updated_by_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who last updated this section. {@link economic_discussion_administrators.id}.

foreignFields.name: deleted_by_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who deleted this section, if applicable. {@link economic_discussion_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Section display name, between 3 and 50 characters. Must be unique across all sections and contain only alphanumeric characters, spaces, hyphens, and underscores.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the section's purpose and content scope, between 50 and 500 characters. Provides context for users browsing sections and helps administrators understand the section's intended use.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was created. Recorded in UTC and immutable once set.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the section was last updated. Automatically updated with each edit operation.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this section was deleted. If null, the section is active and visible. If set, the section is hidden from active listings but remains in database for historical integrity.

models.name: economic_discussion_articles
models.description:
Core article entity storing title, content, section reference, author reference, timestamps, status, comment count, and view count.

Represents user-generated content in the economic/political discussion board. Each article is authored by a citizen, assigned to exactly one section, and may have multiple tags and file attachments through separate tables. Users can create, edit, and delete their own articles, and the system tracks creation and modification timestamps for audit and content freshness.

Articles are the primary business entity that users interact with directly: they create, search, filter, and browse articles across sections. Article views and comment counts are tracked as integer counters for performance optimization.

Article content is stored as plain text with no versioning; edits overwrite previous content. Article deletion permanently removes the record from the database (hard delete).

foreignFields.name: section_id
foreignFields.description: The section to which this article belongs. {@link economic_discussion_sections.id}.

foreignFields.name: author_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who created this article. {@link economic_discussion_citizens.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article title with length between 6 and 200 characters. Required field for article creation.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Full article body text, between 100 and 10,000 characters. Required field for article creation.

plainFields.name: comment_count
plainFields.description: Number of comments associated with this article. Updated incrementally as comments are added or deleted.

plainFields.name: view_count
plainFields.description: Number of times this article has been viewed. Updated on each page load or access.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was created. Always recorded in UTC timezone.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the article was last edited. Updated on every modification of title, content, tags, or attachments.

models.name: economic_discussion_article_tags
models.description:
Junction table managing the many-to-many relationship between articles and tags, with each row representing one tag applied to one article.

Allows articles to have multiple free-text tags and tags to be shared across multiple articles. This table enables tag-based filtering and searching while maintaining normalized data.

Tags are case-sensitive free-text strings up to 50 characters, stored directly in this junction table. The relationship is enforced by composite unique constraint on article_id and tag.

This table has no lifecycle or ownership beyond its association with articles and is only modified when articles are edited.

foreignFields.name: economic_discussion_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article this tag belongs to. {@link economic_discussion_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: tag
plainFields.description: The tag string applied to this article. Case-sensitive, 2-50 characters long. Each combination of article_id and tag is unique.

models.name: economic_discussion_article_files
models.description:
Stores metadata for all file attachments associated with articles, including original name, size, type, and storage location.

This table captures comprehensive metadata for every file uploaded to support articles. Files are stored permanently as long as their parent article exists. Files are managed exclusively through article operations (create/edit/delete) and do not have independent management by users.

File type is stored as MIME type (e.g., application/pdf, image/png) allowing the system to serve appropriate content types and handle different file formats appropriately. Storage location points to the physical file path or cloud storage URI.

If an article is deleted, all associated files are cascaded and removed from the system.

foreignFields.name: economic_discussion_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent article. {@link economic_discussion_articles.id}.

plainFields.name: original_name
plainFields.description: The original filename as uploaded by the user. Required to preserve user's file naming convention.

plainFields.name: size
plainFields.description: File size in bytes. Used for storage monitoring and display to users.

plainFields.name: type
plainFields.description: MIME type of the file (e.g., application/pdf, image/jpeg). Used to determine file handling and display.

plainFields.name: location
plainFields.description: Storage location URI where the file is physically stored, e.g., https://storage.example.com/files/... May include protocol, domain, and path.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the file was uploaded and recorded in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the file metadata was last updated. May be updated during storage migration or metadata correction.

models.name: economic_discussion_comments
models.description:
User comments on articles with content, author reference, and timestamps. Stores all comment metadata including version, status, and deletion information.

Each comment represents a user's contribution to an article's discussion thread. Comments are owned by a citizen user and associated with one article. The system supports soft deletion so that comments can be removed from display while preserving audit trail. Every edit increments the version number for change tracking. Administrator deletions are recorded separately to identify who deleted the comment and why.

Comments are not nested or threaded — each comment is a direct response to an article. They support full text search via GIN index on content. The status field replaces traditional boolean flags to allow explicit lifecycle management with 'active' and 'deleted' states.

foreignFields.name: economic_discussion_article_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the article this comment belongs to. {@link economic_discussion_articles.id}.

foreignFields.name: economic_discussion_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the citizen who wrote this comment. {@link economic_discussion_citizens.id}.

foreignFields.name: deleted_by
foreignFields.description: Reference to the administrator who deleted this comment, if any. {@link economic_discussion_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: The text content of the comment. Must be between 5 and 1000 characters.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the comment was created. Always set to current UTC time upon creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the comment was last edited. Updates on every edit operation.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when the comment was deleted. Null if not deleted. Supports soft delete.

plainFields.name: version
plainFields.description: Incremented by 1 for each successful edit. Starts at 1 for the initial comment creation.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the comment. Valid values: 'active', 'deleted'. This field replaces deleted flag with explicit status tracking.

plainFields.name: deletion_reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the administrator for deleting this comment. Null if not deleted or not provided.

models.name: economic_discussion_comment_reactions
models.description: Tracks user reactions (e.g., 'helpful' votes) on comments. Each reaction represents a single user's feedback on a specific comment.

foreignFields.name: user_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who created this reaction. {@link economic_discussion_citizens.id}.

foreignFields.name: comment_id
foreignFields.description: The comment this reaction is associated with. {@link economic_discussion_comments.id}.

plainFields.name: is_helpful
plainFields.description: Whether the reaction is marked as 'helpful'. True if user voted the comment as helpful, false otherwise.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The timestamp when this reaction was created. Immutable after creation.

models.name: economic_discussion_administrator_requests
models.description:
Tracks requests from citizens to become administrators, including the reason and submission timestamp.

Each request represents a citizen's formal application for elevated permissions within the system. Records remain permanently for audit purposes and are never deleted regardless of approval status.

Requests are submitted by citizens through a dedicated interface and appear in a review queue for super administrators. Each request contains a detailed justification text that explains why the citizen believes they should be granted administrator privileges.

The request is considered "pending" until a super administrator processes it through the companion economic_discussion_administrator_request_decisions table. The request model itself does not track approval status; that state is maintained in the decision table.

This table supports independent operations: citizens can create requests, and super administrators can list, review, and act upon them. Therefore, it has primary stance and requires full CRUD API endpoints for request management.

foreignFields.name: economic_discussion_citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen who submitted this administrator request. {@link economic_discussion_citizens.id}.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the citizen for requesting administrator privileges. Must be at least 10 characters long.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the administrator request was submitted by the citizen. Uses UTC time.

models.name: economic_discussion_administrator_request_decisions
models.description:
Records decisions by super administrators on administrator requests, including approval/rejection status, reviewer, and decision timestamp.

This subsidiary table captures the outcome of reviews performed by super administrators on pending administrator requests.
Each decision record is created when a super administrator takes action (approve or reject) on a specific administrator request.
The decision cannot exist without its associated request, and each request has at most one decision.

The table tracks not only the outcome (approved/rejected) but also who made the decision and when, creating a full audit trail.
It maintains a direct relationship with the economic_discussion_administrator_requests table and references the super administrator who performed the action.
All decisions are permanently recorded and never modified after creation.

foreignFields.name: economic_discussion_administrator_request_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator request being decided. {@link economic_discussion_administrator_requests.id}.

foreignFields.name: reviewer_id
foreignFields.description: The super administrator who made the decision. {@link economic_discussion_super_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: decision
plainFields.description: The outcome of the decision: 'approved' or 'rejected'.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the decision record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the decision record was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this decision was logically deleted (soft delete).

models.name: economic_discussion_bans
models.description:
Stores active user bans with reason, administering administrator ID, and timestamp. References user ID from Authorization Agent's citizens table.

Each record represents an active ban on a citizen user imposed by an administrator. The ban reason must be provided and is stored as a text field with minimum 10 characters as required by the system. This table enables administrators to track and manage banned users through the moderation interface, allowing them to view, search, and unban users. The ban status is managed through the deleted_at field, allowing for reversible bans while maintaining an audit trail.

The reason field is indexed with GIN for full-text search capabilities, allowing administrators to efficiently search for bans by reason keywords. The combination of user_id and deleted_at ensures only one active ban per user can exist at a time.

Banned users' own articles and comments are preserved and remain visible to other users, as required by the business model. This table only controls access to the platform through login denial, not content deletion.

Foreign key relationships link this table to citizens (banned user) and administrators (admin who imposed the ban). Session termination and notification to the user are handled by the authentication service and do not require additional database fields.

foreignFields.name: citizen_id
foreignFields.description: The citizen account being banned. {@link economic_discussion_citizens.id}

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who imposed this ban. {@link economic_discussion_administrators.id}

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason for banning this user. Must be between 10 and 500 characters as required. This field is searchable by administrators using full-text search features.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the ban was created. Always set to current UTC time.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the ban was last updated. Automatically updated on changes.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the ban was lifted (unbanned). If NULL, the ban is active. Used for recoverable bans that can be restored.

models.name: economic_discussion_unbans
models.description:
Records when a previously banned user has been unbanned by an administrator for audit trail purposes.

Each unban event is linked to a specific ban record and documents which administrator performed the unban action with the reason provided. This table serves as an immutable audit trail of permission restoration, allowing system administrators to track when and why access was reinstated after a ban.

No user-facing functionality requires direct interaction with unbans - they are purely operational records for compliance and accountability.

All records are appended only and never updated or deleted to maintain complete audit integrity.

foreignFields.name: ban_id
foreignFields.description: References the original ban record being undone. {@link economic_discussion_bans.id}.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: The administrator who performed the unban action. {@link economic_discussion_administrators.id}.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: The exact moment when the unban action was performed.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: The reason provided by the administrator for unban. This context helps determine if the unban was appropriate or if policy violations occurred during the ban period.
